applicant_utility.summary: This is a single £10,000 tuition-offset award for one Bangladeshi applicant per cycle, not a full ride, so plan to fund the tuition balance, living costs, flights and visa expenses yourself. The scholarship application only opens after you have applied for admission and received your six-digit Cranfield student ID, so treat the course application as step one. Your course must come from Cranfield's 26-programme eligible list and start in September or October of the award year. Draft the four written answers offline, each 250-1000 characters, because the questions probe motivation, career impact, leadership and advocacy in tightly counted characters.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Bangladesh-resident applicants with demonstrable leadership experience targeting one of the 26 listed Cranfield MSc programmes with a September or October start.
application_readiness_checklist: Apply for admission to an eligible full-time MSc and secure the six-digit Cranfield student ID before attempting the scholarship form
Confirm your chosen course appears on the 26-programme eligible list and starts in September or October
Prepare the four written answers offline, each 250-1000 characters, before opening the online form
Budget for the tuition balance, living costs, flights, visa and health surcharge the £10,000 does not cover
Weigh the award against other Cranfield scholarships, since accepting it replaces any other Cranfield scholarship
common_rejection_risks: Submitting a scholarship application before admission is complete and the six-digit student ID is in place
Choosing a course outside the 26 eligible programmes, or one starting outside September/October of the award year
Being a Bangladesh passport holder but not currently resident (or the reverse) - the page requires both
Answers under 250 or over 1000 characters, or answers that present no evidence of leadership experience or potential
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Tuition above the £10,000 contribution, plus living costs, flights, visa fees and the immigration health surcharge - the award only offsets part of tuition.
document_audit: The six-digit Cranfield student ID must already be issued before the scholarship form can be completed
The scholarship form itself is four written answers - admission transcripts and references are handled separately through the course application
No reference letters or extra documents are requested with the form, so do not delay submission waiting for them
alerts: For the 2026 round the window closed at 5pm GMT on Monday 18 May 2026 and Cranfield publishes no advance dates - watch the funding pages from early in the year for the next round
Accepting this award replaces any other Cranfield scholarship, so compare it against Cranfield's other funding before accepting
Outcomes were due by the end of June 2026, so arrange contingency funding around that notification timeline
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Course application and six-digit student ID first, then the online scholarship form (Apply Now) with four written answers, with the university deciding and notifying by the end of June.

applicant_utility.summary: Edinburgh offers three GREAT Scholarships for 2026 across Thailand, Mexico and Ghana, each carrying financial support of a minimum of £10,000 toward a one-year on-campus master's. The published bar is high: the award is made on academic merit and requires the overseas equivalent of a UK first-class honours degree, held or expected. The programme must appear on your country's official eligible one-year on-campus list, which rules out online, part-time and multi-year programmes. The 2026 round has closed and the University says 2027 instructions are coming soon, so set an alert on the Registry Services page rather than relying on aggregator listings.
applicant_utility.best_fit: First-class graduates from Thailand, Mexico or Ghana committed to a specific eligible one-year on-campus Edinburgh master's programme.
application_readiness_checklist: Confirm your target programme appears on your country's eligible-programmes PDF (Mexico, Thailand or Ghana) before applying
Check the programme is one year, full-time and on campus
Secure, or be on track for, the overseas equivalent of a UK first-class honours degree
Be ready to give written consent to British Council contact, briefings, reporting and promotion
Monitor registryservices.ed.ac.uk for the 2027 round opening - no dates are published yet
common_rejection_risks: Applying to a programme that is not on the country-specific eligible list, including online or part-time delivery
Falling short of the first-class-equivalent criterion that the published academic-merit basis requires
Meeting nationality but not residency, or the reverse - the page requires both
Applying before the 2027 round opens, since the page currently publishes no 2027 instructions
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: The award is only a stated minimum of £10,000 and the page does not say it covers everything - assume the remaining tuition, Edinburgh living costs, flights and visa expenses are self-funded.
document_audit: Degree certificate or transcript evidencing the first-class-equivalent result
Proof of nationality and of residency in Thailand, Mexico or Ghana
Written consent to British Council pre-departure briefings, reporting, evaluation and promotion - a condition for successful candidates
No formal document checklist is published on the page; the linked Scholarships Systems FAQs for Applicants PDF explains the application system
